The two arrows leaving C, to B and D, are drawn in accent; the three arrows arriving at C are not counted. The card reads out-degree 2." width="100%"} Out-degree is the number of edges pointing out from the node. Only meaningful for directed graphs. Out-degree tells you how much a node points at others: how many papers it cites, how many accounts it follows, or how many targets a regulator acts on. A node with out-degree `0` is a sink (nothing leaves it). Parallel edges each count, a self-loop counts once, and edge weights are ignored. The graph is not modified. For a summary over many nodes, `aggregate_out_degree()` is more convenient. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node to query, given either as its integer node ID or as its string label (e.g., `3` or `"A"`). A string is always treated as a label. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of outgoing edges. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected, or if `node=` is an ID or label that does not exist in the graph. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~get_in_degree`) : Number of incoming edges. [](`~get_degree`) : Total degree (in-degree plus out-degree). ## Examples {.doc-examples} `A` points to both `B` and `C`, so its out-degree is `2`: ::: {#f98854d3 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C")]) ) graph.get_out_degree("A") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: "B" has no outgoing edges at all: ::: {#3927105f .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_out_degree("B") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 0 ``` ::: ::: Collecting the nodes with out-degree `0` gives the sinks of the graph: ::: {#7e07b0d7 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} [ graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in graph.get_node_ids() if graph.get_out_degree(nid) == 0 ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['B', 'C'] ``` ::: :::
